Caprio|Frank Caprio]] | party4 = Democratic Party (United States) | popular_vote4 = 78,896 | percentage4 = 23.05% | image5 = 3x4.svg | nominee5 = [[Ken Block (politician)|Ken Block]] | party5 = Moderate Party of Rhode Island | popular_vote5 = 22,146 | percentage5 = 6.47% }} {{ElectionsRI}} The '''2010 Rhode Island gubernatorial election''' was held in the US state on November 2, 2010. It was preceded by the primary election on September 14, 2010. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[List of governors of Rhode Island|governor]] [[Donald Carcieri]] was term-limited in 2010. The non-partisan ''[[Cook Political Report]]'', ''[[The New York Times]]'', and [[CQ Politics]] rated the gubernatorial election as a toss-up.{{cite web|url=http://www.cookpolitical.com/ |title=The Cook Political Report | The insider's choice for election analysis |publisher=Cookpolitical.com |date=2010-08-17 |access-date=2010-08-21}}{{cite web |url=http://innovation.cq.com/atlas/gov2010 |title=CQ Politics | Governors 2010 map |publisher=Innovation.cq.com |access-date=2010-08-21 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100611142405/http://innovation.cq.com/atlas/gov2010 |archive-date=2010-06-11 }}{{cite web|url=http://elections.nytimes.com/2010/governor |title=Governor Races - Election 2010 - The New York Times |publisher=Elections.nytimes.com |access-date=2010-08-21}} With 90 percent of the districts reporting on election night, independent [[Lincoln Chafee]] was declared the winner, with 36.1 percent of the vote.{{cite web | url=http://www.wpri.com/dpp/news/politics/local_politics/lincoln-chafee-elected-rhode-islands-next-governor | title=Lincoln Chafee elected RI's next governor - WPRI.com | publisher=wpri.com | date=2010-11-02 | access-date=2010-11-03 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101106012148/http://www.wpri.com/dpp/news/politics/local_politics/lincoln-chafee-elected-rhode-islands-next-governor | archive-date=2010-11-06 }} {{As of|2025}}, this was the last time [[Newport County, Rhode Island|Newport County]] voted for the Republican candidate in a statewide election.
